newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl says mark fully corrected on dollar.
newsitem.headline: Kohl says mark fully corrected on dollar.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl said on Friday he believed the mark had fully corrected against the dollar and that he expected the German job situation to improve in 1997.
Kohl said that the German economy relied on export growth and noted that the higher dollar helped exports.
"It is good to note that the mark has been fully corrected against the dollar in the last year," he told a campaign rally in Frankfurt, held ahead of March 2 local elections.
The dollar today was trading just under 1.69 marks, a rise of 35 pfennigs from an all-time low of around 1.34 marks in spring 1995.

Kohl said record post-war unemployment levels seen in January -- when 4.66 million were registered as jobless -- would improve over the course of the year and the economy would grow by more than two percent.
"In the course of this year we will see a turnaround in the employment situation," he said.
Kohl also said the relatively low German inflation rate would help support economic growth and underpinned the country's social policies.
"Price stability is the best social policy that we can have," he said.
